Meikyuu Kingdom

Meikyuu Kingdom is a tabletop roleplaying game from Japan. It's built around two complementary halves - one in which you play rulers of a kingdom that needs to expand and develop, and one where you delve into a dungeon in order to obtain the resources required for your kingdom.

The players are Landmakers and lead the kingdom to glory, each fulfilling a different role for the kingdom. The Royal is the head of state, the Vizier is the head of the treasury, the Knight is the head of the military, the Oracle is the head of religion, etc. You can also duplicate roles, but since most classes have fiat over certain areas of the kingdom and its people, you can end up with Fun situations if you have two Royals, for example.

Grimdark setting with everyone being undead lolis

Maid Maid is an light comedy anime-themed tabletop role-playing game for three or more players. The very easy to learn rules-light system, complete with random events which drive the story forward, will have you playing the game with friends only fifteen minutes after opening the book.

Tenra Bansho Zero

TBZ is what happens when you take every shonen anime trope and throw it in a blender with Japanese Fantasy and Sci-fi. The results are absolutely insane.

Sword World

Double Cross

Double Cross is pretty much your gritty action/drama anime in tabletop game form. Characters are made into Overeds because a virus is infecting the world, and it's become active within you. Your character has to fight to keep his sanity and humanity while also fighting back Gjaurms (monsters from people who lost their humanity) and rogue Overeds. Interesting mechanics, most of the combat is fluff-based, with just basic addition/subtraction to dice rolls going on behind the scene.

What kind of mic do you use?

I use a Blue Yeti personally, it's a fantastic microphone. Best quality I've heard within that price range.

Currently I use a Electro-Voice N/D767a, which is probably overkill for most people - but I was playing around with different quality problems (EQ, vocal clicks, etc) and thought it would make my life easier. I'm not sure I really like it, the directionality is finicky - but it gets the job done (and it's XLR so I can use hardware EQ rather than having to do it after the fact)
I also use a Blue Yeti and I agree it's a great mic.
Blue Yeti, Affordable mic that is amazing when used properly. (also it is very simple to set up!)

Blue Snowball. I'd considered picking up a Yeti because people kept telling me it's amazing. I ended up seeing the Snowball in a local store for about £20, so I bought it there and then because my headset was giving me headaches. I've felt no immediate urge to replace it in the past 3 years.

We started off with a Yeti Blue. It was a fine mic and works well with one person, but we weren't getting the richness I was hoping for when placed between the two of us. About 6-8 months ago I purchased an XLR mic, the Oktava MK 319, and it is MUCH better in comparison. I like them rich lows, personally, and the Yeti just sounded too empty/tinny if you weren't close enough to it. Recently I just purchased a Rode NTG2 for some video work for a different project we might try out soon. It's a bit overkill for this project but we plan to do more with it than just us sitting on the couch. I did some tests and it seems to give us a bit more freedom with our movements without fear of knocking the stand or sacrificing audio quality.
